experiment: Python+BAML Response.new allocation attribution at 1000 RPS with 2.5-second load and 0.5-second idle cycles
conclusion: The custom BAML rope, PyO3 handle registry, Rust global allocator, and CPython live-object counters rule out a request-proportional retained-object leak in those measured layers. macOS malloc_zone_statistics blocks_in_use grows by roughly 10 to 11 blocks per request, but heap's independent pointer enumeration finds only 1393 additional live allocations without stack logging. Treat blocks_in_use as allocator accounting or retained allocator state, not as proof of 190322 unreachable live allocations.
interpretation: Every explicit BAML collection in the unlogged control returned 80000 live runtime objects after a complete 2500-request burst to one diagnostic response object; the final partial burst returned 64000 runtime objects to one.
BAML rope creation and destruction totals match exactly, so Response.new and diagnostic reporting do not retain custom rope nodes or payload bytes.
The Rust global allocator observed about 1.186 million allocations and deallocations during the control, ending only 102 blocks above baseline. PyO3 live handles ended at zero.
CPython generation-2 collection returned allocated blocks close to baseline and tracemalloc found only 486 additional traced blocks in the control.

The in-process blocks_in_use statistic and heap enumeration disagree by 188929 blocks on their baseline-to-final changes in the control. This makes the in-process block counter unsuitable as the sole leak criterion.

The control's RSS grew mainly during warm-up and then approached a plateau while native threads rose from 16 to 30. The stack-logging run changed concurrency substantially, ending with 108 native threads and 4.24 MiB of extra tracemalloc bookkeeping, so its RSS is intentionally treated as observer-perturbed.
next_measurement: If deeper macOS allocator attribution is needed, enumerate MALLOC_PTR_IN_USE_RANGE_TYPE pointers per malloc zone in-process and compare that count with each zone's statistics callback. A long control should separately record per-zone enumerated live bytes, mapped/resident/dirty malloc pages, native thread count, and pressure-relief behavior.
